claims.statement: The repo-policy-rules conditional recommends repository policies for enterprise lifecycle governance with flexible affected users and targeted organizations/repositories. Recommendation is upstream authority, not an accepted mandatory control or proof of active enforcement; the linked full guide is not reviewed.

The conditional delegated-bypass feature is public preview. Repository administrators request deletion or visibility changes from designated reviewers; approval immediately completes the requested change, denial prevents it but permits a new request. Enterprise or organization owners configure a role/team bypass list. Approval can directly trigger destructive or exposure changes and requires scoped human authority; no list, approval or change was performed.

Policy creation can use Disabled to avoid enforcement or Active otherwise. A stored active setting would still require target, exception and behavior verification; policy existence alone is not enforcement. No activation occurred.

Illustrative policies cover naming such as kebab-case, deletion except by organization admins, public creation restricted to an open-source organization and preventing public-to-private changes to avoid potential metadata loss. These are examples, not adopted names, role grants, required visibility or assurance that all metadata loss is prevented.

The introduction lists five restriction dimensions: permitted visibility for creation and changes, creators, deleters, transfers out of an organization and repository naming. Flexible user/repository targeting is described, not a complete permissions model or verified estate coverage. No repository lifecycle operation occurred.

The public-preview management fragment describes Policy settings bypass-request filters by approver, requester, timeframe and status; Cancelled, Completed, Denied, Expired and Open distinguish cancellation, approved-and-pushed commits, denial, seven-day expiry and unreviewed or approved-but-unpushed requests. Email notifications and a seven-day reviewer window lead to a contributor push or removal of restricted content. This commit-push workflow conflicts in scope with the adjacent deletion/visibility fragment's immediate completion on approval. The mismatch remains unresolved; these statuses are not used as repository-lifecycle completion evidence and no notifications, requests, approvals or pushes of restricted content were performed.
